title_original: What Remains When Home Becomes Memory? Salah Elmur’s Portrait of Sudan

blocks.text: Through painting, photography and personal archives, Sudanese artist Salah Elmur explores the fragile relationship between memory, displacement and belonging in ‘Just as the Heart of a Mango is a Stone ‘ at Jameel Arts Centre, Dubai.

How do we remember a homeland transformed by distance, conflict and the passage of time? In ‘Just as the Heart of a Mango is a Stone ‘ , Sudanese artist Salah Elmur examines the enduring relationship between personal memory and collective history. Bringing together paintings, archival photographs, sketches and ephemera, the exhibition traces his evolving connection to Sudan amid political upheaval and displacement.

Drawing on childhood memories of life near the Blue Nile, Elmur constructs richly layered compositions in which everyday encounters, agricultural landscapes and familial histories intersect with myth and imagination. Central to his practice is the photographic archive of Studio Kamal, his family’s Khartoum studio. By reinterpreting these images through painting, Elmur questions how identities are preserved, transformed and reconstructed across generations.

Curated by Zain Al Saie and Qutouf Elobaid, the exhibition unfolds across three chapters, To Appear Otherwise , Salt of the Earth and Mourning Song , exploring family, labour, grief and belonging. Through Elmur’s distinctive visual language, memory emerges not as a fixed record of the past, but as an evolving space through which histories of Sudan continue to be imagined, questioned and reclaimed.
This exhibition is on view at the Jameel Arts Centre in Dubai until 14 March 2027
